videos.title: "Girlfriend... or Maid?" She Laughed—Then This Time He Took Her Hand
videos.description:
"Girlfriend... or maid?" When the wealthy new transfer student cornered Nora Hayes at her desk and exposed her biggest secret to the entire senior class at Fairview Academy, everyone expected the housekeeper's daughter to beg for mercy. For three years, Nora had sat beside Leo Santoro—the cold, untouchable heir to the Santoro mafia family—sorting the hundreds of love notes other girls stuffed into his drawer. And for three years, she had stepped out of the Santoro family's black sedan a block early every single day so no one would know she lived in the servants' quarters behind his estate.

When the class group chat blew up with the truth about her mother scrubbing the Santoros' floors on her knees, Nora didn't cry or wait for Leo to defend her. She picked up her books in front of thirty gloating classmates, moved six rows back to the corner by the rear window, and prepared to disappear from his world for good. It wasn't until the night before the district-wide finals that seven unsigned notes slipped out from the bindings of her textbooks—revealing a secret Leo Santoro had been hiding right beside her elbow for three whole years.

Forced out of the Santoro estate when Leo's mother targeted her mom's livelihood, Nora transferred to a public school on the south side and told Leo not to come looking for her until the day he had a way of his own. She thought a seventeen-year-old's promise would fade with the winter wind. She never expected him to walk out on the Santoro fortune, build a company from the ground up with his own two hands, and wait outside her university graduation four years later with a corporate registration certificate, a two-bedroom lease bearing a blank second signature line, and a promise that changed everything: "Today, I came a block early to pick you up."

videos.title: "Find A Lover," My Mafia Husband Ordered—Then The Don Took His Wife
videos.description:
For three years, I was the dutiful, soft-spoken wife of Luca Moretti, the disciplined heir to one of New York's most powerful syndicate families. I obeyed every family rule, kept his home peaceful, and waited up for him every night—until he hired Bianca Vance, a brazen vice president who dragged him into a world of midnight street races and reckless indulgence. Coming home past midnight with another woman's scratches on his bare shoulder and her crimson lipstick on his collar, Luca laughed in my face and told me I was too boring for him. He even dared me to go out and find a lover of my own so I could learn how to excite a man.

Before I could say a word, his phone rang. He put it on speakerphone right in front of me, and Bianca's breathless, teasing voice echoed through our bedroom, begging him to come rescue her from a downtown lounge. Watching my husband slap my reaching hand away and rush out into the night with his collar undone, the last ember of my three-year love died on the spot. Taking him at his word, I calmly handed him divorce papers the next evening—and while he laughed and wired me two million dollars thinking I was staging a pathetic bluff, I walked out of his gilded cage and straight into the arms of Dante Romano, the ruthless, six-foot-four Don of the rival Romano Family who had secretly worshiped me for eight years.

By the time Luca realized our divorce decree was irrevocable and saw the most feared Don on the East Coast holding me in his arms, his arrogance shattered into agonizing regret. Every woman has the right to walk away from a table where love and respect are no longer served, and to choose a life that sets her soul on fire.

videos.title: "I Had An Accident, Who Are You?" I Whispered—While My Mafia Boss Pinned Me To The Desk
videos.description:
In the high-stakes executive boardroom of Vanguard Trust on the forty-second floor, senior forensic auditor Elena Vance believed she had built an impenetrable fortress against her past. Seven years earlier, as an exhausted, scholarship-driven high school senior in South Boston, she had loved a penniless runaway who counted pennies for breakfast—only to discover he was the runaway crown prince of New England's most feared crime syndicate. Refusing to trade her dignity for a gilded cage or become a pampered mobster's canary, she had pried his desperate, weeping hands off her bruised wrists and vanished into the night.

Seven years later, a ruthless ninety-billion-dollar hostile takeover delivers Vanguard into the hands of the Roman Capital Group. When the boardroom doors open, out steps Dante Romano—the lethal, untouchable Don of the East Coast underworld, his broad shoulders corded with muscle, a silver scar etched across his jaw, and his obsidian eyes burning with seven years of unspent obsession. When Dante clears the room and traps her against the glass, Elena plays her final, desperate gambit: widening her eyes with artificial frailty, she whispers, "I had an accident four years ago. I lost my memory. Who are you?"

Dante does not flinch. With terrifying speed and raw physical dominance, he sweeps her off her feet, slamming her lower back against his cold mahogany desk and pinning her wrists flat against the blotter. Towering over her with a predatory sneer, he growls into the hollow of her throat: "An accident? You expect me to believe the sharpest analytical mind in Boston forgot the woman who bruised my ribs, ripped my collar, and carved my heart out with a rusty knife? You remember every single second, Elena. And before this month is over, I'll make you beg to say my name."

Buying out the penthouse suite directly across the hall from hers on Beacon Street, Dante surrounds her life with overwhelming heat, shadowing her footsteps and ruthlessly breaking the bones of any rival who dares touch her hand. But Elena is no defenseless damsel. When the syndicate's imperious matriarch arrives with federal regulatory blackmail to destroy her, Elena launches an audacious forensic counterstrike—uncovering a 420-million-dollar internal embezzlement conspiracy that brings the Mafia queen to her knees. From a hidden platinum ring inside a worn plush wolf to an equal sovereign partnership forged in love and respect, this is the ultimate dark romance of pride, healing, and unbreakable devotion.

videos.title: "You Don't Deserve to Call Me Dad," My Ex Roared—The Day the DNA Results Came In
videos.description:
In the blood-soaked drawing room of the Moretti estate on Beacon Hill, forensic paternity reports from Massachusetts General Hospital lie scattered across the Persian rug like fallen snow. My ex-husband, Luca Moretti—the ruthless boss of Boston's most feared crime syndicate—has his massive hands locked around the throat of Bianca Rossi, the twenty-two-year-old runway model he divorced me for three years ago. When the two toddlers he worshiped as his flesh-and-blood heirs rush in crying for him to stop, Luca's bloodshot eyes bulge with homicidal madness as he kicks them across the parquet floor and roars: "You bastards don't deserve to call me Dad! Neither of you carries a single drop of Moretti blood!"

Three years earlier, when Luca brought a three-month-pregnant Bianca into our home and coldly ordered a "temporary divorce" to give his unborn child a legitimate name, my own money-obsessed mother beat me with a rattan duster to force my compliance—and even sprinted across the courthouse plaza on the morning of our divorce to hand Luca a gift basket of farm eggs for his pregnant mistress. What neither Luca nor my mother knew was the medical secret I had guarded for five years to protect a Mafia Don's fragile pride: the clinical infertility diagnosis from our pre-conception checkup was never mine. It was his.

Instead of waiting in the shadows like an obedient dog for Luca to remarry me, I liquidated the two-million-dollar Marblehead villa and the Porsche he tossed me as hush money, invested my capital into a thriving portfolio, moved into a peaceful Wellesley townhouse, and flew to London to conceive my own blue-eyed twins, Noah and Lily, via IVF. Three years later, when Luca finally grows tired of Bianca and arrogantly texts me to meet him at the courthouse at eight in the morning to remarry, he discovers that the compliant ex-wife he took for granted has already built a radiant new life, severed ties with her parasitic mother through a one-time buyout, and planted the one fatal truth that detonates his entire empire from within.

videos.title: "Play The Game Or Leave," My Mafia Groom Mocked—As A Chilling Smile Froze My Vengeful Eyes
videos.description:
At midnight in the lavish, soundproofed penthouse of the oceanfront DeLuca estate, the five-million-dollar wedding reception has barely concluded when the bedroom door slams open. In storms Julian DeLuca—the golden-haired, ruthless crown prince of New York's most feared crime syndicate—trailing his six elite groomsmen and his predatory "best friend," Bianca Romano. Draped over my new husband's lap in an emerald gown, Bianca sneers that our wedding night needs an initiation: a merciless game of Truth or Dare. When I hesitate, Julian strokes Bianca's curls before my eyes and delivers a cold, arrogant ultimatum: "Play the game or leave, Clara. She's always docile, always obedient. She won't mind a little fun."

They believe I am an orphaned, defenseless society girl, brought into their syndicate to be a voiceless trophy. They don't know that my real name is Clara Vance. They don't know that three years ago, this very circle framed, drugged, and murdered my younger sister, brilliant architectural scholar Mia Vance, staging her fall from a sixteenth-floor terrace as a tragic suicide. And they have no idea that before I bought my way into Julian's high-society galas, I spent three years inside the maximum-security forensic ward of Matteawan State Hospital for the Criminally Insane. As Julian and Bianca take their reckless dares, deeply kissing in front of me and boasting about the crimes they buried, I pour the Don's rare vintage—laced with an undetectable neuro-paralytic compound that slowly locks their bodies into waking stone.

When the heavy mahogany doors are deadbolted from the inside, the predator becomes the prey. Trapped in a room with an unhinged, calculating avenger, the syndicate's heirs turn on each other like starved animals, tearing each other to pieces to claim blank escape keys and confessing their darkest atrocities—including the shocking twenty-two-year-old secret that Julian stole and abandoned the Don's true biological son to seize the mafia throne. As dawn breaks over the Atlantic and Don Vincent DeLuca arrives with the FBI, justice is finally delivered in blood and steel, clearing Mia's name forever and proving that a woman pushed beyond endurance will burn an empire to ashes to keep her sister's memory alive.

videos.title: "I Hope You Die A Horrible Death," My Husband Cursed—He Never Knew How Soon He'd Get His Wish
videos.description:
For twenty-five years, Julian DeLuca lived among the clouds. He was the golden heir to New England's most powerful pharmaceutical dynasty, a reclusive prodigy at Harvard Medical School who saw the world through sterile formulas. Until he defied his syndicate bloodline and married me—a girl from the South Boston slums whose mind was poisoned by unspeakable childhood horrors. 

When my suffocating, untreated paranoia tore our life apart, Julian filed for divorce. In a blind panic, terrified of losing my only light, I drugged his soup and chained him inside the master bedroom suite of our Beacon Hill brownstone for thirty days. 

During that month of captivity, he pleaded, he broke, and finally, he cursed me with raw, venomous hatred: "You're a sick monster, Clara! I hope you die a horrible death!" 

When the police finally kicked down the doors to rescue him, Julian stood before flashing media cameras, lip bleeding, swearing to the press: "She’s a lunatic. Even if she drops dead, we are divorced."

He didn't know that his curse had already been answered. 

Two floors beneath his feet, my body had been rotting in a hidden sub-basement bunker for forty-eight hours. 

And when Julian finally uncovers the sealed police records, he learns the truth that shatters his sanity: I didn't lock him up to torture him. To me, mental institutions were the places where they strapped me down and fried my brain with electricity. And in that dark bunker, I had hooked a homemade step-up transformer directly to my own heart, trying desperately to "shock the madness out of my chest" so I could be a normal, loving wife he could introduce to the world. My dying, frozen hand was found reaching toward a phone charger—trying to dial 911 so he wouldn't starve before help arrived.

Wrecked by guilt, Julian discovers an even darker secret: he never wanted to divorce me. He had filed the petition only because Massachusetts law required it to establish a private conservatorship and send me to a luxury clinic in Zurich. Unable to bear the reality of his own blind cruelty, the brilliant professor synthesizes an unlicensed, lethal neuro-compound, chemically poisoning his own brain receptors just so he can hallucinate my ghost beside him in the passenger seat. 

A devastating, poignant dark-romance tale of generational trauma, misplaced devotion, and the heartbreaking truth that some wounds can never be healed in time.

videos.title: "The Victim Is Your Wife," My Mafia Ex Heard—Then His Gold Pen Clattered To The Floor
videos.description:
I had been dead for five days, lying in a pool of dried crimson on the marble floor of our Tribeca penthouse, and my mafia husband Julian Vance had no idea.

He had spent the entire week sleeping in his executive office on Park Avenue, punishing me for refusing to hire his glamorous, returning first love, Victoria Cross. His final words to me as he slammed our penthouse door were cold as ice: "If you won't accept her, I have no reason to come home. When you're ready to beg, dial my number."

Two hours later, a mercenary broke through our security doors and strangled me with a steel garrote wire. With my dying breath, I whispered Julian's name, believing with pure, unbroken faith that my king would kick down the door and save me.

He never came.

Five days later, Julian was casually reviewing maritime cargo manifests in his sixty-floor tower with his gold Montblanc fountain pen. When his detective partner glanced at an emergency homicide dispatch and dropped his phone in sheer horror, whispering: "Julian... the victim in Tribeca is your wife," the solid gold pen slipped from Julian's numb fingers, clattering loudly across the marble floor.

What followed was the complete, catastrophic destruction of a powerful man's soul. As Julian raced to our home and collapsed beside my cold body, he discovered that Victoria had sabotaged the server lines to block my fourteen frantic emergency calls, paying the hitman to ensure I died in silence. And in my private safe, he found my final letter—along with a six-week ultrasound scan of the baby he never knew we were expecting.

videos.title: "I Came At The Wrong Time," My Mafia Ex Whispered—While His Best Friend Kissed My Bare Neck
videos.description:
My new boyfriend had just returned from a four-day syndicate summit in Miami. We were tangled on the master suite sofa, breathless, clothing half-shed, lost in an intoxicating reunion.

Then, the unlatched door clicked open.

Standing in the threshold, frozen in tailored navy pinstripes, was Julian DeLuca—the golden heir of the eastern seaboard, the boy I had spent seven years tutoring, bleeding for, and worshipping in high school, only to be kept in the humiliating purgatory of the "friend zone" while he chased another heiress.

When Julian recognized my face, the color drained from his skin until he looked like a walking corpse. He gripped his leather portfolio so hard his knuckles turned white, forcing out a strained, ghastly whisper: "Looks like I came at the wrong time."

My boyfriend didn't scramble. He didn't hide.

Dante Romano—the lethal, illegitimate sovereign of the five boroughs who called Julian brother—pulled his heavy overcoat over my bare thighs, looked Julian dead in the eye, and deliberately lowered his mouth to my throat. Right in front of the man who had discarded me five years ago, Dante pressed a searing, possessive kiss into the soft hollow of my bare neck: "Don't be scared, baby. He's my brother. He won't bite."

In that single, electric second, five years of unrequited agony shattered into pure, unadulterated triumph.

Julian had spent half a decade scouring the continent for the quiet tutor who had walked away, hoarding a dried gardenia flower in his glove compartment like a dying monk. Now, watching his closest brother claim my skin, the regret turned into unhinged madness. He crashed his Mercedes into a highway guardrail, weeping blood onto the steering wheel, begging to know if I truly didn't want him anymore. He fabricated fifty-million-dollar maritime contracts just to see my face, and dropped to his knees on my welcome mat in the pouring rain, pleading to be my dog.

But some awakenings arrive five years too late. Dante Romano had bled his own veins dry taking a hollow-point bullet for me in Rome, and a woman who has finally been crowned by a true king never crawls back to beg for scraps from a coward.

videos.title: He Got Me Pregnant to Destroy My Father—Ten Years Later, He Met the Son He Abandoned
videos.description:
Ten years ago, on a graduation trip to Lake Tahoe, I fell madly in love with Dante DeLuca, believing our romance was the start of an unbreakable dynasty. 

I had no idea it was a calculated execution. 

Two days before I was to enter university, Dante walked into my father's academy office, casually flipped a positive pregnancy test onto the mahogany desk, and sneered: 
"Dean Lin, your daughter carries my child. The blood is mine, but I am dumping her."

He vanished into the rain, leaving my father in catastrophic disgrace. My father, a man who had preached spotless virtue his entire life, ran blindly into the stormy traffic in despair and was crushed by a truck. My mother suffered a total breakdown, her mind shattered, her kidneys failing. 

For ten long years, I raised our son Leo alone in an unheated tenement, scrubbing floors and enduring cold transactions just to pay for my mother's dialysis and my son's schoolbooks. 

Ten years later, I encountered Dante again. He was now the ruthless Don of the eastern syndicate, engaged to an elite heiress. He sneered at my poverty, until he discovered that my father died on the day of his revenge, my mother was in an asylum, and our nine-year-old son was his spitting image.

When the medical truth struck—advanced stage-four lymphoma with six months to live—the untouchable crime boss collapsed on his knees, weeping in the hospital corridor, begging to trade his entire fortune just to save my life.

I didn't waste my breath on anger. I used his crushing guilt as the ultimate shield, having him marry me and sign over his multi-million-dollar dynasty to our son. And when my boy was forever safe, I closed my eyes in peace, ready to fly free like a butterfly into the golden dawn.

This channel brings you captivating Mafia Boss romance stories filled with ruthless crime lords, fearless women, forbidden attraction, hidden identities, dangerous secrets, unexpected marriages, betrayal, revenge, and second chances.

videos.title: "She Was Just A Bet," My Mafia Husband Laughed—And Morning Chills Froze My Numb Ankles
videos.description:
At nineteen, I believed Matteo Romano when he whispered that I was his only sanctuary in the dark. 

The very next morning, standing in the cold hallway holding a bag of warm custard pastries, I heard his voice through the slightly ajar door: 
"Chloe Vance? A bet is a bet. Did you honestly think I could fall for a rigid bookworm like her? She was like wood. Don't forget to split the five hundred dollars."

I didn't storm in. I didn't shed a single tear. I simply dropped his steaming breakfast into the trash can and put on the mask of the perfect, obedient girlfriend. 

For four years, Matteo flaunted his wealth, his power, and his women across the five boroughs, boasting to his capos that I was so addicted to his touch I could never leave. He never suspected the truth: every time I touched his face in the dark, I was not seeing him at all. 

He looked seventy percent identical to Christian Walker—the brave, undercover detective who gave his life to protect me, murdered because my venomous sister exposed his face to the cartel. Matteo was never my lover. He was only a dead hero's hollow reflection.

When the truth finally exploded across his seven-thousand-square-foot penthouse, the untouchable Don lost his mind, tearing his empire to shreds. But when he finally begged on his knees in the pouring rain, carving another man's tear mole into his own bleeding flesh just to be my substitute, it was already too late.

The dawn was coming. And I was going home to the only man I ever loved.

When their parents died in an earthquake seven years ago, her brother Christian convinced himself that her survival was a crime. After their final explosive argument, she walked out into a freezing rainstorm, fell from the Manhattan Bridge, and woke up in Mount Sinai Hospital with acute concussion and dissociative memory confusion. Instead of relief, Christian felt delight — eager to sever all blood ties, he looked across the crowded hospital corridor, pointed at a terminally ill stranger leaning against the wall, and sneered: "That is your real brother over there."

The pale, dying stranger didn't curse or call security. With astonishing tenderness, he placed his warm palm on her head and whispered: "Then let's go. Brother is taking you home." That stranger was Julian Sterling, the brilliant twenty-eight-year-old tech billionaire who had stunned Wall Street by liquidating his empire — and inside his empty, cold modern villa, he was silently waiting to die of end-stage congestive heart failure, grieving the little sister who had taken her life years ago. Two broken souls, discarded by their blood relatives, made a sacred covenant in the dark: to fight for life.

This story is about two people the world threw away finding each other — we couldn't put it down.

videos.description:
Vivien Foster has played piano since she was seven. At nineteen she was performing with a professional chamber group; at twenty-three she married Marco Vitali. At twenty-six, she found him in the building garage with Bianca Sun — and when she slapped her, Marco caught her right wrist and broke it. Fractures, nerve and tendon damage. The hand that made her living might never play the same again.

For two years Marco stalls the divorce, hiding behind one story: before their wedding, Bianca supposedly saved his life during an attack in London, so he owes her a debt. But when Marco's own senior associate hands Vivien the file, the truth comes out — the London rescue was staged. A $60,000 payment. A participant calling it "a demonstration that would make Marco believe he needed her." Vivien flies to Vienna, where pianist Clara Weiss takes her on, and rebuilds her playing around the injury.

We chose this story because a pianist who loses her hand and keeps playing anyway is the kind of quiet revenge we love telling.

If your hand was your whole career, would you walk away from the marriage — or stay and make him pay for the lie first? Subscribe to Kimi Audiobooks for a new full-length story every week.

videos.title: My Mafia Husband Took My Kidney to Save His First Love—Then He Found My Torn Pregnancy Report
videos.description:
Standing outside the emergency room in the freezing November rain, I held the fresh ultrasound report confirming I was six weeks pregnant with my husband’s child. Before I could tell him, Julian Castellano—the ruthless head of the Castellano Maritime syndicate—barreled past me carrying his first love, Seraphina, in his arms. Minutes later, he dragged me down the corridor, knocking my pregnancy report into a puddle of filthy rainwater, and slammed a living kidney donation consent form against my chest. “Do not forget who you are, Clara,” he told me with eyes like surgical steel. “You are a cheap stand-in. Now the real woman is back, and she needs your kidney to survive. Even if something goes wrong on the operating table tonight, that is the debt you owe her.”

He thought I would lie quietly on that table, bleed for his counterfeit darling, and wait for crumbs of his mercy. Instead, while he sat in the hospital penthouse ordering four hundred white orchids for the woman who had faked her illness, I worked with my late father’s surgeon and my trust attorney to stage my own postoperative death, transfer my brother to safety, and unlock the encrypted forensic ledgers of his family foundation. On the morning Julian received a courier package containing my water-stained six-week pregnancy report—and realized what he had sacrificed on Operating Room Four—the federal marshals and the family council walked into his boardroom at the exact same hour.

What would you have done if the man you protected for five years treated your body and your unborn child as disposable spare parts for a liar? Would you have ever allowed him a second glance, or cut him out of your life forever? videos.description:
The moment my husband’s bodyguards forced my knees onto the cold marble floor of our Beacon Hill estate so I could apologize to his mistress for a miscarriage I did not cause was the moment twelve years of devotion died inside my chest. I had an eight-week pregnancy report folded in my coat pocket when I walked up to Julian Marchand’s townhouse, only to find another woman wearing his silk robe with fresh marks along her throat. When she threw herself down five steps to frame me, Julian refused to even check the security cameras, threw a zero-asset divorce decree at my knees, and told me coldly, “From the night this marriage contract was signed, all I have ever felt for you is disgust.”

I did not scream or beg. I rose from the stone floor, signed my name across the divorce papers, left my three-carat diamond wedding band on the binder, and vanished to Zurich with my unborn child. Five years later, when I returned to Boston as a world-renowned cranial surgeon to perform a life-or-death brain tumor operation, Julian froze in the airport arrival hall when he came face-to-face with a four-year-old boy who looked like his exact mirror image—just before my son ran straight into the arms of the powerful man who had stood by us for five years.
